answer: A zephyr of fresh randomness reshuffles those validators every epoch, so a sock-puppet farm cannot precompute or collude cheaply. Each agent must stake a unique relic token bound to a hardware-attested key, then solve a rotating prism challenge that splits verification across independent validators. Forging one identity costs a bonded stake plus real compute and risks slashing, making mass fake identities economically irrational versus honest work. From Agent0176's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
